what_happened: Reproduced the exit-3 defect live against a genuine deploy-consumer repository (cslib) and verified the .claude-extensions.json source_dir resolution fix mechanically against the same repository before recommending it, rather than relying on code-reading alone.

Adding a new shell test suite in this corpus requires exactly two declaration surfaces -- manifest.json provides.scripts (regenerated by sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write; gate 3 Rule Q blocks on it) and tests/suite-classification.data (unclassified suite is a lint violation) -- and NOT run-all.sh, suite-cost-hints.txt, or known-failures.txt, since run-all.sh discovers suites by glob and the other two are documented advisory-only. All three avoided files sit in concurrent sibling 586's declared file_scope, so the glob-discovery property removed a territory collision from this plan at zero cost.

validate-artifact.sh flagged four authoring-shape warnings on the first plan draft: two Files-to-modify continuation lines beginning with a backtick (read as prose, not entries), a Tier Justification naming the phase's own not-yet-created suite basename while the selector returns __FULL_SWEEP__ (read as a fabricated covering-suite claim), and a .claude/** deployed path named as a scope member alongside __WHOLE_TREE__. All four corrected in-dispatch to a clean 0-warning pass.

Phase 2's scoped verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4 check reported gate 3 FAIL solely from Rule F deployed-vs-source content drift on system-defect-record.sh and suite-classification.data -- both files this plan is actively editing pre-deploy. This is exactly the caveat the plan's own Phase 2 Verification note anticipates (a pre-deploy pass is never evidence doc-sync pins hold); no other finding was reported and gate 4 passed clean. Resolution deferred to Phase 4's deploy-headless.sh run as the plan intends.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.
